name: Nippur scribal school
description: Boys copied sign lists and Sumerian literature onto clay tablets in a school called the edubba.

name: House of Life
description: Temple scriptoria trained scribes in hieratic writing, medicine, and astronomy.

name: Songlines and Country
description: Aboriginal knowledge of land, law, and stars passed down through song, story, and ceremony.

name: Plato's Academy
description: Students learned mathematics and dialectic through dialogue. It closed by edict of Justinian.

name: Taixue imperial academy
description: Han emperors trained officials in the Confucian classics, the root of the later examination system.

name: Nalanda mahavihara
description: A Buddhist monastic university that drew students from across Asia for debate and logic.

name: House of Wisdom
description: Baghdad scholars translated Greek, Persian, and Indian texts into Arabic and extended them.

name: Al-Qarawiyyin
description: Founded in Fez, it taught law, grammar, and astronomy and still operates.

name: Whare wananga
description: Maori houses of learning taught genealogy, navigation, and ritual to selected students.

name: University of Bologna
description: A guild of students hired lecturers in law. It is the oldest continuous degree-granting university.

name: Sankore Madrasa
description: Timbuktu scholars copied manuscripts and taught Islamic law and mathematics.

name: Calmecac
description: Aztec nobles' children studied priesthood, astronomy, and law in strict residential schools.

name: Yachay Wasi
description: Inca nobles learned quipu record keeping, Quechua, and history in Cusco.

name: Harvard College
description: The first colonial college trained clergy through Latin, Greek, and logic.
